goroutines.title: Goroutines
goroutines.description: Goroutines are separate jobs, not a promise of one desk per job. Let three jobs finish, and compare that with main returning before it waits.
goroutines.html:
Goroutines are separate jobs, not a promise of one desk per job. Let three jobs finish, and compare that with main returning before it waits.

  • Count the goroutine lanes on the stage while the loop runs
  • Say what wg.Wait() does for main
  • Predict what might print if you delete wg.Wait()

creation.title: Creation
creation.description: Launching work is like writing the address on an envelope before sending it. Change the original variable after launch and inspect the argument the new job…
creation.html:
Launching work is like writing the address on an envelope before sending it. Change the original variable after launch and inspect the argument the new job received.

  • Say when the new goroutine's value gets its copy of n
  • Explain why changing n after the go line does not change value
  • Pass a value as an argument to give a goroutine its own copy

the-gmp-scheduler.title: The GMP scheduler
the-gmp-scheduler.description: Scheduling is matching jobs, workers and permission slips. Move the pieces together before asking why a goroutine is different from a thread or a core.
the-gmp-scheduler.html:
Scheduling is matching jobs, workers and permission slips. Move the pieces together before asking why a goroutine is different from a thread or a core.

  • Say what G, M and P each stand for
  • Explain why a goroutine is not the same thing as an OS thread
  • Say what runtime.GOMAXPROCS(2) asks the runtime for

run-queues-and-work-stealing.title: Run queues and work stealing
run-queues-and-work-stealing.description: An idle worker can look for tasks on another workbench. Step through ready queues before deciding whether idle means there is no work anywhere.
run-queues-and-work-stealing.html:
An idle worker can look for tasks on another workbench. Step through ready queues before deciding whether idle means there is no work anywhere.

  • Say the difference between runnable and running
  • Watch which goroutine gets the next turn when one finishes
  • Explain why real Go does not promise this print order

preemption.title: Preemption
preemption.description: A long speaker needs a way to give others a turn. Compare the work timeline with preemption enabled and with a deliberately restricted teaching schedule.
preemption.html:
A long speaker needs a way to give others a turn. Compare the work timeline with preemption enabled and with a deliberately restricted teaching schedule.

  • Say what preemption lets the scheduler do
  • Explain why main waits at <-done while the loop runs
  • Say why preemption does not make shared writes safe

networking-and-the-netpoller.title: Networking and the netpoller
networking-and-the-netpoller.description: Waiting for a delivery need not leave a worker staring at the door. Follow a simulated outside event and see which waiting task becomes runnable.
networking-and-the-netpoller.html:
Waiting for a delivery need not leave a worker staring at the door. Follow a simulated outside event and see which waiting task becomes runnable.

  • Say what a parked goroutine is doing while it waits (nothing)
  • Explain how main wakes up when the value arrives
  • Predict which of two sleeping goroutines sends first

timers-and-sleeping.title: Timers and sleeping
timers-and-sleeping.description: A timer is an alarm attached to a waiting job. Advance virtual time, wake the job, and stop a repeating alarm when its work is finished.
timers-and-sleeping.html:
A timer is an alarm attached to a waiting job. Advance virtual time, wake the job, and stop a repeating alarm when its work is finished.

  • Say what time.Sleep does to the goroutine that calls it
  • Explain why this simulation prints exactly 5
  • Read the virtual clock before and after the sleep
